utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Judge Fluegge is, for urgent personal reasons, unable to continue sitting in this case today, and it is likely of a short duration. Judge Moloto and myself, we have decided that it would be in the interests of justice to hear -- to continue the hearing of the case in the absence of Judge Fluegge. And it can be foreseen that the same situation will exist for the whole of this week. Of course, the Chamber is aware that we cannot continue for more than five days in the absence of Judge Fluegge. Any matters to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I have two brief matters. I'd ask that we go into private session for them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rave. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Rave.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I did not tender 1D888. I forgot to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. We can no longer hear Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against admission of 1D888.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D888 receives number D274, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D274 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we briefly see 1D885 in e-court now. That is a transcript from the Tolimir case. It is Mr. Franken's testimony. We need page 70, which should correspond to 3472. That would be the transcript page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will see here that when Mr. Tolimir asked him -- actually I'm going to read this out in English, from line 13 onwards: [In English] "Did you ask" -- I quote: "Did you ask for specific targets to be stricken or did you just ask for a blanket support? "A. On the risk that it is getting technical, but we did both, in fact. We gave all the hardware -- sorry, all the known targets being guns and artillery and mortars and tanks, et cetera, we put them on the list and gave them a free-for-all, a killing zone, so to say, directly south of Srebrenica, and that is the area between the city of Srebrenica and generally Zeleni Jadar." [Interpretation] Are you aware that members of your battalion provided intelligence as well, in terms of marking the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska for future NATO air strikes.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they provided the information for future NATO air strikes. I think that all our troops provided the information where they [Realtime transcript read in error "rarely"] saw the VRS in the southern part of the enclave. That was collected in the OPs room, and it's up to them to decide either to put it on the list, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Rave. I would request that you repeat your answer. You are recorded as having said: "I think that all our troops provided the information rarely saw the VRS." I don't think that makes sense. Could you just look at the transcript and correct it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. All our troops in the enclave, so all the UNPROFOR soldiers that were aware of VRS troops in the southern part attacking either the Muslims or UNPROFOR troops were reported. So, of course, you can say that they were normal troops but it is a kind of gathering intelligence where the enemy is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that at the time, in that area, there were also members of UNPROFOR, British nationals, who guided NATO aircraft to targets?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm aware that within the battalion we had the -- I don't exactly know the name, but the guys who were educated to guide aircrafts on targets. We had them in our own battalion, and I know that some of our regular platoon guys did it in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're moving on to the 11th of July, 1995. Is it correct that you, of course, together with the other members of the Dutch battalion, decided to move people from Srebrenica to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I told you yesterday, I think we talked to the commander of the Bravo Company in the town of Srebrenica, Mr. Boering and myself, when the UN facility was so overcrowded that we had no possibility that the people could stay there, that we had to try to get them northward to the Potocari area. And I don't know if we decided it ourselves or there was information from the higher levels in Potocari to do so, but I know we did, and I'm not sure that we had a direct order to do so, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise for pausing slightly. Yesterday I was cautioned about the fact that I did not wait for the interpretation to be over so there are quite a few things that are missing from the audio recording. So please do bear with me. It doesn't mean that I'm not satisfied with your answers. I'm just waiting for the interpretation to be over. At the time, there were air strikes against VRS positions; right? The 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't think there were air strikes. There was close air support, so specific targets, because there's a big difference between air strikes and close air support.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- please, please, no loud speaking. Everything has been fixed? I do understand it has been fixed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You spoke about shells that were falling by the column that was moving towards Potocari. Do you know who fired these shells?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not sure, of course, but I only can imagine it was the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This column that was moving towards Potocari, were all people walking in a single direction or were some people trying to move in to a different direction?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they all were moving in the northern direction. And, of course, there might be a single person who went back, to find the rest of his family or anything else. But the column, in general, was moving forward in a northern direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, how many such shells fell?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to give exact numbers. I only know that during the period I moved from Srebrenica towards Potocari, some shells fell and, well, at least more than two or three, but I can't exactly -- give you numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment, you did not know where the members of the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Because the evening of the 10th, we saw lots of people in military clothes moving in a northwestern direction, and we hardly didn't see any military-clothed men during -- on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When speaking to the Serb side, you also noticed that they did not know where the soldiers of the 28th Division were; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I mentioned it. The only thing I know is that all the time we spoke to General Mladic at that time or to others, they wanted to know where they were, the men of the 28th Division, and they wanted to have contact, and we were not in contact at that moment with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The destination of that column was Potocari, or was it the intention of the people in the column to go via Bratunac further on?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't imagine that it was their goal to go further on because Bratunac was a Serb territory. The only thing they wanted was safety and security. They had the imagination that they could find it on the UN compound, so, in my opinion, they only wanted to go to Potocari to get the UN protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because you said that the fire was intended to prevent the people from going further. In fact, their intention wasn't really to go further on but to reach Potocari; right? I'm merely explaining the reason why I put that question to you.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be. And I think when there was a shelling between Potocari and Bratunac or Yellow Bridge, at the moment, it was an extra motivation for them not to go further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are Serbian positions right beyond the Yellow Bridge; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Yellow Bridge, in the hills were Serbian positions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now us to look at P1147. It's a video, V000-926. We need to see several sequences and stop at 22:36 minutes. Can we have that? And then stop at 32 minutes, 39 seconds. [In English] 32:36. Or -- yeah, yeah, please, we can start with 31:19. [Interpretation] And we'll proceed on to 32 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that General Mladic's intention and order was to head for Potocari and Bratunac. And we're on the 11th of the July, 1995. Do you know that, on that day, one could not reach Potocari along that route? The Army of the Republika Srpska could not because of the armed attacks mounted by the 28th Division. Instead, General Mladic had to go back to Sase, and, from there, he went to Bratunac and then to Potocari. In other words, on that day, the Srebrenica-Potocari road could not be used. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're giving a lot of information or evidence, I do not know what it is, and then you ask, Were you aware of this? Is that only limited to the last portion? Then you should have left out all the earlier information. If it includes the earlier information, you have to go step by step, and then ask whether armed attacks were mounted by the 28th Division -- you have to -- you can't just tell a long story and then say, Do you agree that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can -- I can make that long story short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Army of Republika Srpska was not able to make it along the Srebrenica-Potocari road on -- on that day?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Short answer: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like us to play the same video from 32 minutes, 36 -- 36 seconds. Can we play it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know - and we were able to see it in this video - that somebody opened fire at General Mladic on that day, on the 11th, in Srebrenica? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see on the video is -- what we see is a picture of Mr. Mladic and we hear shooting and behaviour such that apparently there's some concern that they may be the target. That is what we see. Nothing more, nothing less. You should not interpret the evidence for the witness and then ask whether he is aware of what you apparently see. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, remain seated. Mr. Mladic -- remain seated, Mr. Mladic. And no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you know that, on the 11th of July, in the town of Srebrenica itself, there were still members of the 28th Division present?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to the first meeting at Hotel Fontana, one that you attended as well. You tell us that General Mladic was angry on that occasion. Was he blaming the DutchBat members for the casualties that NATO aviation inflicted on the VRS troops that day?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my recollection, he was blaming DutchBat as being the ones who asked for the air strikes and who were responsible for killing his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were telling us about threats, the threats that General Mladic made against you and Mr. Boering, the way you understood them to be; right? This cannot be seen in the footage that is an exhibit in this case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I know he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since it was Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans who suggested that there be air strikes, the fact remains that he could have asked for air strikes once more; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, of course, can you ask whatever you want. You're more or less -- you say it was Karremans who suggested that there be air strikes. The fact remains that he could have asked -- of course, you do A and you could have done perhaps a different thing. You could have done B or C. That's not a question. It's asking, more or less, for judgement, opinion, rather than for facts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A factual question would have been: Do you know whether he has considered to do -- ask something else, for example. That's a factual question. And might provide you the information apparently you are seeking but then in an appropriate way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You heard the guidance given to me by His Honour Judge Orie. Did you know if Mr. Karremans had the intention of asking for more air strikes?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, of course, but I don't think that he had the intention to ask for more air strikes, because we lost the war at the moment and it was impossible to ask for more air strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The reaction on the part of General Mladic seeking that there be no more air strikes and his concern at that point, were they real?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you should ask General Mladic why he estimated that -- that concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking for judgement or opinion, Mr. Lukic, which you are supposed not to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that he was angry and made threats, General Mladic explicitly told you - and this can be seen in the footage - that UNPROFOR and civilians were not the target of the Army of Republika Srpska. And you do recall that part, do you not?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that's in the same video when he threatened us that: This will not be your last cigarette. Do you want to see your family again? We were happy. You have only one life. So it's a mix of all those things that created the situation, especially at that moment. Not being aware of the role of General Mladic at that moment, in what direction he wanted to go, that's -- in our opinion, at least in my opinion, there was a threat, and I still had the -- the feeling in the first ten minutes that there would be a possibility to put us in the garden and shoot us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic should remain seated. Again, Mr. Mladic, you should remain seated. One. Second, you should not react in any way on the testimony given by the witness. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were telling us about this meeting and the sound that you heard, which you believed to be coming from a pig that was being slaughtered in front of the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was in the second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D905?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with the document; you've seen it before. It was in the Tolimir case. It's a document issued by the Drina Corps Command on the 10th of July, 1995, where approval was granted for the slaughter of cattle. And, under 2, it is stated that permission is granted for the slaughter and delivery for the needs of the UN soldiers billeted in the hotel in Bratunac of hogs or pigs, weighing up to 80 kilos. Do you know what were the facilities available to Hotel Fontana for that purpose? Was it ... so do you know what sort of sanitary conditions existed in Hotel Fontana, whether this is something that they normally did whenever Hotel Fontana would receive a supply of livestock, in fact?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the way the -- the Serbs in this area provided the hotel with stock or anything else. I don't know how they fed our POWs who were there. But the only thing I can say that if it was food for the UN soldiers, it might be perfect, but I don't think it's perfect to slaughter the pig on an open window during a meeting. You should have done that by daylight the day before or the day after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it, in fact, your case, Mr. Lukic, that Hotel Fontana slaughters pigs in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, Your Honour. I'm just trying to establish with the witness. We'll probably have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, I'm saying is it your case. Is that your case? Yes or no. It's not your case, that's not what you're trying to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking the witness if he knows what's the procedure. If he is claiming something, he should claim it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not answering my question, that's fine. Thank you so much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like us to look at a video-clip, which is now P1147, V000-9266. We need 15 minutes, 4 seconds, and 15 minutes and 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You recognise these soldiers in the footage as DutchBat troops; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that some of them were filmed outside of the hotel and the others in one of the dining-rooms. Or, at any rate, there seemed to be tables there. This is my question: When you came to the Hotel Fontana, you were allowed to see the DutchBat soldiers. It was Major Boering who saw them before the meeting, and then you yourself saw them after the meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw in the video how they comported themselves. Was it your impression that they were relaxed, that they did not feel their life was at risk?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they were relaxed. There was not a tense situation when we entered that room. But the only thing they wanted to know: What's going on, and what will happen with us? That was the main question of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D886 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your evidence in the Tolimir case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page number 41 in e-court. We need -- or that corresponds to page 6776 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in lines 6 and 7, after giving a rather long answer, starting from line 1, you say in line 6 and 7, [In English] I quote: "And what he told them and what I later on saw that they looked rather relaxed because they really didn't know what was going on." [Interpretation] Does this refresh your memory that you believed them to be relaxed when you saw them? Or at least that was your evidence in the Tolimir case.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think we can translate "relaxing," they didn't feel threatened at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The members of the DutchBat left their observation post, right, at one point, and tried to retreat deep within the Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Muslim forces did not allow them to do this; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The -- they prevented us to do the job in the way we wanted to do it. Because, in a normal military way, when you are in a position, and either you're firing on -- on an enemy and you try to take another position, then you go backward, find a new position, and they prevented us to do so. That was the reason why they didn't go backward but forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was seriously and under threat that the Muslims prevented the DutchBat troops from retreating; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For that reason, since the threat was a serious one, the DutchBat soldiers surrendered to the Serbian forces; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, not a single soldier of the DutchBat was killed as a result of fire coming from the Serbian forces; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the same time, one of the DutchBat soldiers was killed but as a result of fire coming from the Muslim side; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the soldiers on the OP Foxtrot returned from their OP and wanted to go back to the compound, the road was blocked in the -- the dirt road towards the compound was blocked, and Muslim civilians tried to stop the APC and, in the same way as I told you, the Muslim army did, because they only had one goal: The UN should go forward and fight the VRS. That was their impression. When the APC passed the group of Muslim civilians, either a hand-grenade was thrown or a shot was fired, and that caused the death of one of our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, civilians were also armed.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know, in that period at least, and -- civilians on the Muslim and the Serb side, most of them were armed. Although in the area - and I think that's the direction you want to go - there were still a lot of weapons, although we did our utmost to disarm them, to demilitarise the enclave. We didn't manage. And we didn't manage to demilitarise the Serbs, although it was not our task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The civilian who shot and killed the Dutch soldier, was he within the column? How did it happen? Was it someone throwing a hand-grenade out of the column? Can you describe this for us? How did this death of a Dutch soldier come about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again, you should take it step by step. Earlier the testimony was, when the APC passed the group of Muslim civilians, either a hand-grenade was thrown or a shot was fired and that caused the death. So, therefore, it has not yet been identified who fired the shot or who have thrown the grenade. In your follow-up questions, you already imply answers on questions that have not yet been put to the witness, such as the civilian who shot and killed the Dutch soldier. Let's first establish whether the witness knows whether this shot was fired from that group of civilians or whether the hand-grenade was thrown from that group of civilians. Mr. Rave, are you -- do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the hand-grenade or the shot came from the group of the civilians at the end of the dirt road from OP Foxtrot towards the main road to Potocari. It was not -- there were no civilians that were in the column because it was some days before. I think it was the 8th or the 9th, but I have to take a look in my notes. So it was not on the 10th or the 11th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say -- when you said a grenade was thrown or a shot was fired when passing the group of civilians, you say, That shot was fired from that group of civilians or that hand-grenade was thrown by a person in that group of civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we have established it. We take it step by step. Please proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help. I think it's time for our break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break. But we'll first ask the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at five minutes to 11.00. Perhaps, Mr. Lukic, perhaps briefly discuss with your client that the Chamber does not accept any comments or reactions on the testimony, which is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Groome, the matters you raised in private session at the beginning of this session are taken care of. And it's partly translation; it's partly redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are we more or less on track, which will mean that you would conclude today?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would there still be left some time for Mr. Jeremy, then? Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope so. I hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You hope so. Mr. Jeremy, could you give us an indication as to -- as matters stand now, whether you would need much time or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I would say between five and ten minutes, at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, to the extent you could accommodate Mr. Jeremy and the Chamber, you're invited to do so. We'll now continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly like to ask to have the witness's microphone switched off when witness is not speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also noticed, perhaps I make a comment there, that once the microphone of the witness is switched on, that there is a rumble. There is a lot of background noise. So apart from the witness switching off his microphone if he is not speaking, I would have rather have it resolved by technicians as well and not to remedy it in the way as we are doing at this moment, but to start with it would be okay. Then please proceed, Mr. Lukic. And the witness is invited to activate and deactivate his microphone, as requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to go back briefly to the sound that you heard in front of the Fontana hotel. When I showed you 1D905, and this was the approval for the slaughter of livestock, I want to put the Defence case to you. The Defence asserts that this was done in one of the facilities of the Drina Corps. According to the information we have, the noise came from the following. One of the members of the VRS kicked a dog that was in front of the Fontana hotel. Now this is my question for you: Can you claim with certainty that the noise did not come from a dog? Are you certain that it came from a pig that was being slaughtered?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some things. There might be a dog kicked in front of the hotel. I told you that we were in the briefing room or in the meeting room that the window was opened. It was not the front side of the hotel, it was the back side of the hotel. I don't know the area over there. The only thing I know that the window was opened. I know the sound of a pig that was slaughtered. I recognised it as a pig that was slaughtered. And after some minutes, the window was closed. So don't mix up front and back of the hotel, and I think I can make the difference between a dog and a pig.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I did not express myself properly, in front of the hotel or behind the hotel. At any rate, we have testimony stating that someone below the window kicked a dog several times. However, if you're saying -- actually, I think that the answer is a bit confused. That it may be a dog but that you think it's a pig. Is that it? Would that briefly summarise the answer that you provide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness says, I can make the distinction between a pig and a dog. He says it was a pig. So he doesn't say, It may have been a pig. Let's take his -- whether you believe it or not, whether you have evidence which contradicts it, fine. No problem. But let's not change what the witness told us. At least if I understood you well, Mr. Rave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. And let's not -- it is a relatively small element.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why I was confused, I just want to point that at page 23, line 18, there is a sentence: "There might be a dog kicked in front of the hotel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What the witness says is that beyond what he could hear in front of the hotel and he said he couldn't -- he had no view, he had no -- it was not within hearing distance. Whether someone kicked a dog over there he wouldn't know. But what he heard was a pig after the windows were open. That is clearly the evidence the witness gave. And, again, if there's any contradicting evidence, the Chamber would love to hear it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Then I will leave the topic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know that the Dutch battalion ordered skis and that an attempt was made to transport that into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came in in January. Then there was bit of snow, but I don't know if in that period skis were ordered, maybe to do some sports or anything else. But after that, for sure not because it was so hot, there was no snow, and I don't know why they used skis in summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- actually, you don't know at all whether there had been any ordering or not and whether there had been any subsequent transport so we're not going to go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just need a still from P1147 now. V000-9266. We need the 4th minute, the 53rd second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to remind you what we're talking about. As you will see, this is a conversation. You do remember this moment, don't you --

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- when people in uniform and also a man in civilian clothing is talking to the members of the battalion. Do you know who these uniformed men belong to? Do you know whether this is the army or the police?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is the army, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, I'm going to tell you that these are members of the police. And in the footage we saw two men in addition to the interpreter and that is Raso Pantic and Dusko Jevic and they are members of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Lukic giving evidence or is Mr. Lukic presenting what is agreed between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I assume he presenting what is agreed into the -- by Mr. Ivetic. These people are identified in the stills book as members of the special police as opposed to the municipal police. And I believe that's what he would be doing, although we haven't spoken about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Now I'd just like to ask for something from the same video, P1147, that is, V000-9266. From the 23rd minute and 54th second, up until the 25th minute and the 32nd second. It is the presence of General Mladic in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said to us that food had been brought to the civilians and that its distribution was halted once General Mladic left. Had everything been distributed, everything that had been brought in? Or was something brought in and then taken away? I'm speaking about food, water.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was brought in. The only thing I know that I saw in that area that General Mladic was providing some bread and I think some chocolate to the refugees. I haven't seen him bringing water, and for the people inside the compound at least that there was brought nothing. Maybe there is evidence that we can see that Colonel Acamovic [phoen] some days later is negotiating about convoys coming in, but the only thing that General Mladic at that moment brought was some bread. He made a show in front of the camera. Then left and the distribution of the bread they had with them stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that all the bakeries in the region were involved and that everything that could have been made on that day was brought in? Did you have information about the quantity of bread that could have been made in that area at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that bread was even brought in from Serbia because the local bakeries could not bake large quantities?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But as I say, just as the buses, General Mladic asked us for buses because they were not available. Now in this video he is stating that he organises the transport and he organises the buses, so ... it doesn't say anything to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Rave, could I invite you not to comment on the questions, et cetera. You were simply asked whether you knew about Serbian bakeries assisting because local bakeries couldn't do. That's the question. You could limit your answer to that. I would have, however, one additional question. You said you don't know what was brought in. What did you see, in terms of quantities of bread? Because you're talking about bread and chocolate. Are we talking about ten loaves? 500 loaves of bread? Approximately, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw approximately 50 loaves of bread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the demilitarisation of the enclave. So first I'd like to show you D17. The essence of your testimony in this aspect is that there were no organised military structures in the enclave of Srebrenica. This is a document of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Command of the 28th Division, and this is a document dated the 30th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D17.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what can be seen here is that a few days before the start of Krivaja 95, the Command of the 28th Division is sending a report to the Command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. And it says here that soldiers of the 28th Division of the land forces located in Srebrenica and Zepa decided to give the largest possible contribution to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in its fight against the aggressor, and with that aim, they intensified their activities deep inside the territory temporarily occupied by the aggressor. Did you know that in official documents of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, they actually call the Bosnian Serb army the "aggressor army"?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here - it's in these bullet points that we see further on - the results achieved are being listed and in the first group it says that 13 Chetniks were killed. Did you know that in the official documents of the Army of Bosnia members of the Army of Republika Srpska are being called "Chetniks"?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the last bullet point it says: "Several dozen Chetniks were wounded." And then, number 2 says: "In order to prevent enemy forces from sending additional forces from the Srebrenica and Zepa areas to the Sarajevo theatre, two acts of sabotage were carried out near Srebrenica, on the 23rd of June at Osmace and on the 23rd of June at Bijelo Stijenje, near Koprivno, and the following results were achieved: Seven Chetniks were killed ..." And then number 3. It says that on the 26th of June 1995, several successful acts of sabotage were carried out deep inside the territory temporarily occupied by the enemy and, as a matter of fact, 20 to 40 kilometres deep in the area of Han Pijesak and Vlasenica. And then there's a reference to Visnjica, Crna Rijeka, and the Vrani Kamen feature. Now on the next page in B/C/S, and it's the same page in the English version, the last bullet point states that over 40 Chetniks were killed in these actions. What were the positions that you personally held within the Dutch battalion? You were in charge of security, were you not? And, at the same time, you were the liaison officer for communication with the civilian authorities and the military authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As security officer, in order to make the right decisions, was it indispensable for you to know the information that is contained in this document of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it would be very interesting for us to have these kind of documents but we were not in the chain of command of the BiH army. But maybe I can add something, because, of course, we heard lots of those rumours frequently from the VRS side, especially from Major Nikolic. All the time they told us that BiH or whatever who went out of the enclave to commit actions in whatever form, we got never the proof that, A, they happened; B, we got not the freedom of movement to go out to check it. We got not the equipment to do our job properly inside the enclave so that we could check at all. So I think you've got some answers now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ask -- after these accusatory allegations made by the Serb side, did you ask the Muslim side whether they were, indeed, carrying out such actions?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, we asked. And, of course, the answer was no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for me to follow. Mr. Lukic, you've shown a document where there's internal reporting within the Army of the BH structures. You refer in your question to: "Did you ask after these accusatory allegations made by the Serb side ..." Is that specifically in relation to these events described? Or what -- what's the factual basis for those allegations by the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because this gentleman already testified that Captain or Major Nikolic complained and also another VRS officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But not specifically on these events but more on general terms. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: More of general terms. But such a -- like events and the actions like these performed by 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You give them as examples --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which may have been covered by a general allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you said to us that demilitarisation had not been carried out in the enclave of Srebrenica and Zepa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. I said that one of our tasks was to demilitarise the enclave of Srebrenica. We were not in Zepa. In Srebrenica the demilitarisation started with the Canadian battalion. After that, the three Dutch battalions did whatever they could to disarm the population and the parts of the 28th Division or the 28th Group. We did our utmost. We collected lots of weapons, but, at the end, it was shown that we were not able to disarm the enclave completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we had a rather lengthy examination of a witness about demilitarisation - I think it was in relation to Gorazde - where we had to look at quite some documents on -- on what exactly was the -- was the legal situation. Is it the same here or is it different or ... could you assist us in referring to where we find the demilitarisation tasks and how it was decided by the UN?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know it by heart, but I know that we have documents as -- as an evidence in this case. It's two agreements on Srebrenica and Zepa demilitarisation. One -- both from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have the numbers, then that would sufficiently guide me to find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have ERN numbers in front of me. I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said they were in evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have the ERN numbers, perhaps Madam Registrar could assist us. Could you please read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are two. One from May, 8th of May, 1993, and ERN is 01239650. English version is R1024231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you can confirm that this is in evidence or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It should be D15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D15. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll have a look at D15.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Stewart tells me it's also in under P23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D15 is something different. It says: "Debrief of UNMOs from the Srebrenica enclave dated 24th of July."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's check the P number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to find a better one. I'll have a look at P -- Meanwhile, you may continue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you do remember that there was an agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before most of the military forces left Srebrenica, you saw a great deal of armed and uniformed people within Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you ask someone where they got the weapons from? Did you have time to do that?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Specific answer: I could have find the time, but I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the shipment of the weapons to Srebrenica via Zepa? The weapons reached Zepa by air.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if weapons reached Zepa by air, but I also don't know about the shipments from weapons to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now briefly look at a document, 1D893.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since the B/C/S version is a poor copy, let me tell you that it's a newspaper article, an interview with Naser Oric issued by the Sarajevo paper "Oslobodjenje" on the 23rd of August, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English version on our screens only so that we can follow. The headline or the title of the text is: "Weapons that were handed over were out of order." We need page 2. We will look at the portion beneath the subtitle: "Demilitarisation of Srebrenica." It is stated here that Naser Oric said, and that's paragraph 1, line 3. [In English] I will quote in English. "When the order of demilitarisation came, the commander told me to deliver only those weapons which were out of order and useless and heavy guns because we not hide them. So I did. We kept the defence lines and our weapons. "So we handed over to the UNPROFOR only some of the weapons. For instance, two tanks. We had five tanks, but since we had not had fuel for them, we had to burn some down, so we kept only two and withdraw [sic] them into the depth of our territory." Then the fourth paragraph in this section says, I quote: "Most of the weapons we surrendered were useless or almost useless. We kept the rest." Then we'll have to go to page 3 in English. Fourth -- or fifth paragraph from the top. I quote: "Sefer Halilovic intervenes ..." Then the second row, the end of the row. I quote: "I order you to deliver the weapons that were out of order. It was approximately, including those homemade and useless rifles, 200 barrels all together, plus some heavy weapons that you could not hide ... at the same time, you had a plan how to recapture the weapons, if necessary, from the UNPROFOR." Now, the next title is: "Guards along the lines." And the third line says, I quote: "We had some 2.000 barrels. I know that for sure. And I did not know everything. Weapons were being hidden. We kept some 20 cannons, for sure, with four barrels." And the last sentence in -- in this paragraph, I quote: "So we had probably some 4.000 barrels and it became manifest during the breakthrough towards Tuzla, let alone the brigade of Zepa ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As security officer, did you have information to the effect that at the time when you were in Srebrenica, the 28th Division had, as stated by its commander --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel repeat the number of barrels or rifles he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know about the amount of weapons they had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- the interpreters ask, first of all, whether you could repeat the number of barrels. Is that 4.000, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's 4.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4.000. Yes. Were you aware, did you have information that there were 4.000 -- probably 4.000 barrels in Srebrenica held by the forces of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were aware that a lot of people inside the enclave still had weapons. When we saw them with weapons, we confiscated them, but we didn't know about any numbers. And, as you can see in the document, not even Naser, as commander of the operational group, knew how many weapons there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this would also have been the information that you had to have in order to make proper decisions as a security officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What kind of decisions are you referring to, Mr. Lukic? Could you be more precise in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman was supposed to make a decision or give a suggestion to the commander of the DutchBat as a security officer on what should be done next and in what way, who should be monitored and in what way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have known that information of -- of probably 4.000 barrels, would that have been useful in your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think that the amount of barrels is important. We knew that we had to demilitarise the zone. We were not able to do so, and we didn't get any other means or the possibility either to check, for example, all the houses. So it didn't change anything when I knew even the amount of barrels that there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said you had to demilitarise. I had a look now, Mr. Lukic, at P23 where it's about demilitarising, but the -- who has to do what may need further attention before we continue to talk about demilitarising and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naturally. Of course, I didn't mean Mr. Rave in person, but I meant that this was one of the main tasks of the DutchBat in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it on the basis of P23? I mean, we're talking about demilitarisation. Who has to do what. That is, for me, as we earlier did in -- for different areas -- because looking at P23 - but forgive me when I'm wrong - going through it very quickly, it seems that the parties accept an obligation to demilitarise -- they're to hand over their weapons and that UNPROFOR is a witness to that and plays a role that they will accept weapons which are handed over to them. It is an agreement between two parties. So, therefore, the task described there, although as a witness, but is mainly, at least going through it very quickly, UNPROFOR shall take the handed-over or submitted weapons in custody. UNPROFOR shall take the handed-over submitted ammunition in custody separately. It -- from what I read at this moment, it's not, You should confiscate weapons. And therefore my question to the witness would be: On what basis did you confiscate weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of demilitarisation, when we saw people outside houses with weapons, we confiscated the weapons. They got a ticket that we confiscated the weapons and we stored them in the Weapons Collection Point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you did. But on the basis of what? On the basis of what instrument or the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as my knowledge goes, it was on the basis of the task we had in the mandate in -- demilitarise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, perhaps we have then to look in more detail to the mandate. But when I earlier asked for the demilitarisation, then I -- if I look at the document, that raises, at least, a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will ask the witness, though I believe that he referred to it, in part, just now.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was in our mandate to demilitarise but not to chase and to search houses to demilitarise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was precisely going to be my question. You didn't have the mandate to search houses, and you've answered to that. You were able to and did react only when you saw someone out in the open carrying weapons in the town of Srebrenica. This is another thing that you told us about. However, I will now read to you from another passage of this interview with Naser Oric. It's the same document we have here. The last paragraph. What is discussed here is how they went about tricking you, in fact, deceiving you. [In English] "As soon as the UNPROFOR set up their check-points, we realised that we could not rely upon them. So one team of my men, who had no military education but were reliable and who made part of reserve units, decided to establish our lines. To organise our monitors. The system functioned in the following way. When an UNPROFOR patrol was approaching, our guys on the lines informed us so we could remove the weapons. If the UNPROFOR soldiers asked about presence of our boys on those lines, we answered that we could not trust them and that we were afraid of Chetniks so we wanted to have our guards. They showed some understanding for that, which was not the case when we dug trenches and fortifications." [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that, since you were foreign to the area, you didn't speak the language, the Muslims in Srebrenica found it very easy to trick you and conceal weapons from you, to deceive you?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't too difficult to conceal weapons, and I think it has nothing to do with the language because we had interpreters. But in an area - and I think you have been there - as big as it is, it's no problem at all to conceal some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's speak about the offensive combat activities that the Muslims mounted out of Srebrenica. One of the topics is the linking up of the enclaves. At that time you were there, were you aware that the road between Srebrenica and Zepa was under the control of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm even not aware about a road between Zepa and Srebrenica because the enclave of Srebrenica ended for us at OP Echo. We were not able to build more OPs because the VRS denied us to bring in more material to build OPs to control more of the southern part because, of course, there was a lot of complaints from the VRS side that there was a traffic between the enclave of Srebrenica and Zepa. We were not able, because it was a very big terrain, to control it all. And specifically a road, there wasn't a road. There were a lot of dirt roads through the woods, and I don't know what road you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have knowledge to the effect that Srebrenica and Zepa were two enclaves that were not linked together? Were you briefed on that? And that you - and that's to say the Dutch battalion - had only Srebrenica under its control and not Zepa?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And they were not linked because between Zepa and Srebrenica were the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Krivaja 95 operation was launched precisely for the fact that what you just said was not true? That's to say, that the Serbs were not present on the road between Srebrenica and Zepa, they didn't have it under their control, and that that was the main objective of Operation Krivaja 95.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that with this operation you mean the takeover of our OP Echo in the southern part of the enclave and they wanted the road that was going from east to west, in my opinion, and not from north to south or south to north. And the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa were north/south, and the road they wanted to use was the east/west road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If would you inform the witness what you mean by Krivaja 95 because, otherwise, I think you're talking at cross purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Krivaja 95 is an operation launched by the Army of Republika Srpska in order to separate the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. Were you at all familiar with the contents of that order?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that order. The only order I know is the -- the takeover of OP Echo, and I don't know if it was part of this operation, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to tender 1D893 into evidence before we move on to the next document. It's the interview given by Naser Oric and Sefer Halilovic for the Sarajevo newspaper "Oslobodjenje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness doesn't know anything about it, isn't it? Do you want to tender it from the bar table or through this witness? What is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may. I think the witness confirmed that he knew about some amount of the weapons concealed inside the enclave. But here we have more precise data so it's not even contradicting what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think our rule is that if the witness testified about a matter of -- or about an issue on which we have evidence, although the witness is not aware of that documentation, that that might be a reason not to wait with bar tabling this evidence but, rather, then tender it immediately. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just to confirm: The length of the pages is four pages in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I moved from that document. Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar seems to confirm --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, four pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No objections to the tendering of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D893 receives number Exhibit D275, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D275 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, we'll take a break in approximately two or three minutes from now. If there's anything you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can finish one more document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so that we are able to plan our scheduling for our next witness, I wonder if Mr. Lukic could give us an estimate of his remaining cross-examination time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but I think that probably I need an hour, a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An hour, a bit more, which would bring us -- it might leave us 15 to 20 minutes at the very end, as matters stand now. So, therefore, if the witness is there, I'd like him to remain stand by, and with the apologies if he will be called only tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That's understood, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic, for your last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the break. Not the last document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can have 1D904.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or, rather, the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. The 29th of April, 1995, is the date. The heading says: "Per your request, instructions for further action in connection with UNPROFOR's intention to set up an observation post in Srebrenica." The document is sent to the Command of the 28th Division, the army, the land forces. The second paragraph, under number 3, says: "Bearing in mind the above mentioned, and fully understanding the serious negative consequences of the possible setting up of an observation post of UNPROFOR for the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina (threatening the Zepa corridor) we suggest the following." Actually, my introductory question to you would be as follows. Is it correct that beforehand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, isn't it true that we have two sets of numbers here and that you were reading from page 1, the first 3, rather than the follow-up 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because we are now guided to the second page in English where we still have to remain on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First page; first number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it correct that beforehand in that location, there was an observation post and that, for some reason, it was abolished and then an attempt was made to reinstate it there?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware exactly of the location at this moment. Lozine, is it in the western part of the enclave or in the southern part of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously this is an observation post that would threaten the Zepa corridor.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I stated, Zepa is in the southern part of the enclave, and I think that sometimes we tried to establish a new observation post over there, but the problem was we didn't get the clearance to bring in the material. And, of course, it was quite simple because when we were there and everybody asked us to be between the two parties, we tried to establish observation posts as possible between the parties. And I don't have the imagination that the BiH caused problems when we would create an observation post in the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I think it's time for break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. Could the witness follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, when I'm insisting so much on the legal text underlying demilitarisation, or whatever, I hope that you'll understand that it may make a difference whether you violate something you have agreed upon voluntarily as a party to an agreement or whether you violate any provision imposed by the Security Council. That's the reason why, when we are talking about what parties are supposed to do, why I'm so insisting on having the proper legal basis available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To answer shortly to Your Honours, I guess it was regarding the -- the agreement on demilitarisation of Srebrenica in -- in Article 5, if we have P23 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to deal with it with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then fine. Then if you say, Could you specifically read paragraph 5 of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll read it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. And it's -- we need second page in English. It's second-last paragraph inside the paragraph 5, non-combatants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But did you want to deal with it with the witness. I said I will read it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, there's no reason to have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had it on the screen for a long time, my own screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I will move on, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on, Mr. Rave?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] You saw this document, and the village of Lozine is mentioned in relation to the corridor. It's in the south of the Srebrenica enclave; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, the name Lozine doesn't ring a bell at this moment. I should take a look at the map. But when it is in the south, then I stay to my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we'd like to take a look at document -- actually, I would like to tender this previous document, 1D104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess it's 904.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 904. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D904 receives number D276, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D276 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D809 [as interpreted]. That is the document we'd need in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This, roughly, is a document with a content that is similar to the previous one. However, here, the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the 17th of June, 1995, is issuing an order to the Command of the 28th Division of the Land Forces. And the heading is: "Preparations for offensive combat operations." In paragraph 1, and paragraphs 2 and 3, we can see the content of the order, which is basically an order to prepare operations that would be carried out outside the enclave. In conversations with members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina within the enclave, did you receive any information to the effect that these forces were commanded on some occasions by the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina directly?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously this document shows that this is part of a wider military operation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Might be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, at that time, attacks were being launched from the city of Sarajevo with a view to breaking through the Serbian ring around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that because we're talking now on the level far above us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time, you received intelligence -- you had intelligence concerning the locations of tanks of the Army of Republika Srpska, the locations of cannons, positions, and we saw that from the testimony that we put to you today, Mr. Franken's testimony. Did you have any information about where cannons and tanks were within the enclave, the ones that Mr. Oric spoke of?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. Because, otherwise, when it was possible, we have confiscated them and stored them in the Weapons Collection Point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again now, the previous question, you said: "At that time you received intelligence" - it's unclear whether you're referring to the witness or to DutchBat - "you had intelligence concerning the locations ... and we saw that from the testimony that we put to you today, Mr. Franken's testimony." This Chamber still has to determine whether what Mr. Franken told in another and which was put to this witness, whether that is accepted for a fact, yes or no. So the way in which you introduce your questions is not the way you should have done it. Could you please keep that in mind. Facts are only facts once the Chamber has evaluated all of the evidence. Please proceed. Or when they are agreed between the parties, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did I put to you today something that came out of the testimony of Mr. Franken that you would not agree with?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I can't remember exactly what came out of the testimony of Mr. Franken, but I think, within my possibilities, I answered all your questions, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] Did you receive intelligence, you as a Dutch -- as the Dutch battalion only from your own sources or did you also use sources outside of the Dutch battalion, such as UN or perhaps NATO sources?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you gather intelligence, you get your own intelligence, and, of course, you use all the intelligence that is available. So also reports from our higher echelons gave us intelligence and information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Terrain observation in and around Srebrenica was done through several means, unmanned aircraft, laser surveillance, or personal observation on the part of the members of the Dutch battalion; right? You had all of these at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we hadn't this at our disposal at all. We had our personal observations, and, as I told you, we have the reports and the intelligence that came from the higher echelons, but we didn't have those means at our own disposal, within the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. You should whisper. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Bosniak side, the Muslim side, tried to bribe members of the DutchBat into not reporting on the weapons that were detected and into allowing the supplies of weapons to come into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at 1D883, another document connected to this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the Command of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Republic of Bosnia and -- Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated the 8th of July, 1995, which was precisely the time when the VRS operation directed at Srebrenica began. It's a report on combat results of the units and commands of the 28th Division of the land forces of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Under bullet point 1, it is stated that 60 Chetniks were killed, "and, according to unconfirmed reports, the aggressor suffered even greater losses and had many wounded." It's yet another operation of the 28th Division outside of the enclave of Srebrenica. Beneath the bullet points, the following paragraph reads: "In the village of Visnjica, large quantities of ammunition were seized but the soldiers were exhausted and could not pull out more. Therefore, the ammunition was destroyed as were all the facilities that the aggressor could have used for military purposes." Do you know that, at that time, a heinous crime was committed by the BH army in this village where all the houses were torched and the entire population was killed? Did you have this sort of intelligence?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing I want to answer that the attack on the enclave was not started on 8th of July but before, when OP Echo was targeted. I think then started the operation to go into the enclave of Srebrenica. And further on, I'm not aware of the things you just mentioned that are in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it took you three minutes and a half to introduce a question, just are you aware of a horrible crime committed in Visnjica, which -- and then we are not here to educate the witness about what is contained in the reports of the BiH but we are here to hear his evidence. Three and a half minutes you took it to set out where the question was answered in the negative, so there was no need to do that. Please proceed, and keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that the operation by the Serbian -- Serb forces began earlier. But can we then agree that, at the same time as the VRS operation commenced directed at Srebrenica, the forces within Srebrenica not only were capable of mounting a defence but also of mounting offensive activities outside of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the attack on OP Echo started, we tried to deter the attack. At that same moment also operational activities within the enclave from the Muslim side took place. We tried to stop them, tried to avoid it, because we didn't want to level the tension more than it was already. So we tried to get in contact with both parties and both parties to stop the confrontations from both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the question was a different one. The question was whether, at the time, as you said, the operation -- the Serbian operation started, whether you were aware of the Muslim forces undertaking operations outside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only awareness we had was the information we got from the Serb side that they told us that the Muslims were taking actions out of the -- outside the enclave. But that's the only thing we were aware of, told by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order and others like it issued by the BH army is not something that you ever seen; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, did the members of the 28th Division that you held meetings with in Srebrenica have the duty to show such orders to you?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ask them to show you the plans and effects of their military operations?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE [Resumed]
